ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is a coordinate graph of changes in the vegetation growing season in urban fringe areas. The vertical axis represents the number of days of the vegetation growing season, and the horizontal axis represents the distance from the urban edge (km). The legend shows four curves for Shanghai City, Nanjing City, Hangzhou City, and Changzhou City. The four curves overall all show that the number of days of the vegetation growing season is greater in places closer to the urban edge, and as the distance from the urban edge increases, the vegetation growing season overall decreases or is relatively shorter. Then reason: The length of the vegetation growing season is closely related to heat conditions; higher temperatures will lengthen the frost-free period and the time suitable for plant growth. Due to factors such as buildings, roads, population activities, and energy consumption, cities and their fringe areas often have temperatures higher than surrounding suburban or rural areas; the farther from the city, the weaker this warming influence is. Therefore, the pattern in the fringe areas of the four cities in which the growing season is longer near the urban edge and gradually shortens outward may be caused by the urban heat island effect.
